title: Implement TOC part parser (part 0 / part 1 file listing)
description:
Implement parsing of Table-of-Contents parts in src/toc.rs.

Background: Some multi-part UUencoded posts include a TOC as part 0 (or occasionally part 1). The TOC body is plain text listing the constituent files, their sizes, and part spans. Conventions vary widely; this parser should be best-effort, not strict.

Public types:

  pub struct TocEntry {
      pub filename: String,
      pub size_bytes: Option<u64>,
      pub parts: Option<std::ops::RangeInclusive<u32>>,  // which parts carry this file
  }

  pub struct ParsedToc {
      pub entries: Vec<TocEntry>,
      pub raw_text: String,   // kept for diagnostics when parsing is partial
  }

Public function:
  pub fn parse_toc(body_bytes: &[u8]) -> Option<ParsedToc>
  // Returns None if body_bytes does not look like a TOC at all
  // Returns Some(ParsedToc) with partial entries if some lines parse and others don't
  // Never returns Err — best-effort parse

TOC line formats to handle (document formats found in MIME-zjr.1 research):
  - 'filename.tar.gz   1234567 bytes   parts 1-8'
  - 'filename.tar.gz (1234567 bytes)'
  - '01-08  filename.tar.gz  1234 KB'
  - Lines starting with '#' are comments: skip
  - Blank lines: skip

Heuristic: a body qualifies as a TOC if at least one line parses as a TOC entry AND the part containing it has part_number <= 1 (i.e., it is part 0 or part 1).

Tests (oracle: hand-constructed TOC text samples from real Usenet archives or documented formats):
  - Full TOC with 3 files, correct entries extracted
  - TOC with unparseable lines — partial result, no panic
  - Body that is NOT a TOC -> None
  - UTF-8 filename in TOC entry — should not panic
  - size_bytes parsed correctly (bytes, KB, MB variants)
  - Part range extracted correctly from 'parts 1-8' and '01-08' formats
